Proposition
[Symmetries of the Curvature Tensor] 1. ch7:7.12

Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian manifold. For all vector fields $W,X,Y,Z$, its $(0,4)$-curvature tensor satisfies

  1. $Rm(W,X,Y,Z)=-Rm(X,W,Y,Z)$.

  2. $Rm(W,X,Y,Z)=-Rm(W,X,Z,Y)$.

  3. $Rm(W,X,Y,Z)=Rm(Y,Z,W,X)$.

  4. $Rm(W,X,Y,Z)+Rm(X,Y,W,Z)+Rm(Y,W,X,Z)=0$.

Identity (d) is the algebraic Bianchi identity. In any local frame, the symmetries are egin{align*} R_{ijkl}& =-R_{jikl},& R_{ijkl}& =-R_{ijlk},\ R_{ijkl}& =R_{klij},& R_{ijkl}+R_{jkil}+R_{kijl}& =0. \end{align*}

Proof

\sketch Part (a) follows from $R(W,X)=-R(X,W)$. For (b), metric compatibility gives

egin{align*} WX|Y|^2& =2\langle abla _W abla _XY,Y angle +2\langle abla _XY, abla _WY angle ,\ XW|Y|^2& =2\langle abla _X abla _WY,Y angle +2\langle abla _WY, abla _XY angle ,\[W,X]|Y|^2& =2\langle abla _{[W,X]}Y,Y angle . \end{align*}

Subtracting the last two equations from the first yields $Rm(W,X,Y,Y)=0$; polarization in $Y,Z$ proves (b).

For (d), symmetry of the connection expands the cyclic sum as

egin{align*} R(W,X)Y+R(X,Y)W+R(Y,W)X & =[W,[X,Y]]+[X,[Y,W]]+[Y,[W,X]], \end{align*}

which vanishes by the Jacobi identity. Finally, apply (d) to the four cyclic arrangements of $W,X,Y,Z$, add the resulting equations, and use (a) and (b); the uncancelled terms give $2Rm(Y,W,X,Z)-2Rm(X,Z,Y,W)=0$, which is equivalent to (c).
